faq.lead: Quick answers about reporting drug activity, getting help and joining prevention programs.
faq.q1: What can I report, and do I need proof?
faq.a1: You can report anything you've seen or heard that you think is drug activity, such as selling, using in public, storing or transporting drugs, or drugs near a school. You don't need proof. Share what you know, including where and when. Please don't confront anyone or put yourself at risk.
faq.q2: Do I have to give my name?
faq.a2: No. You can report completely anonymously under our ZERO LOG policy. No name, phone number, or personal details are required or tracked unless you explicitly choose to share them for official follow-up.
faq.q3: What happens after I submit a report?
faq.a3: Your report is securely routed to the National Operations Joint Intelligence Desk. Qualified officers evaluate the intelligence, coordinate inter-agency verification, and mobilize law enforcement or community interventions accordingly.
faq.q4: Is it safe to ask for help with drug use?
faq.a4: Yes, absolutely. Calling Hotline 1927 is 100% confidential and medical-first. You or your family will receive guidance on certified inpatient and outpatient rehabilitation therapies without fear of legal prosecution.
faq.q5: How can I volunteer or organize a prevention program?
faq.a5: You can join as a community volunteer or youth ambassador through the Citizen Portal or your local Divisional Secretariat. We provide verified educational materials, workshop guidance, and institutional support for schools and villages nationwide.

cta.statement: Know about drug activity? Report it. You can stay anonymous, or share your name and contact details so officers can follow up with you. Report online or call 1818 toll-free. Available 24/7 across all telephone networks in Sri Lanka.

about.metaTitle: About Initiative | Ratama Ekata National Operation
about.metaDescription: Vision, Mission, and Objectives of the Ratama Ekata National Operation against drug abuse in Sri Lanka.

header.title: A drug-free, safe Sri Lanka.
header.description: Sri Lanka’s united national initiative bringing together state institutions, security forces, and citizens to eradicate drug trafficking and safeguard future generations.

vision.title: Vision
vision.text: To protect Sri Lanka’s most valuable resource—its future generations, particularly children and young people—from the dangers of drugs and build a safe, healthy, and drug-free society.

mission.title: Mission
mission.text: To unite government institutions, security forces, and the public to reduce drug supply and demand, disrupt drug trafficking networks, strengthen prevention and public awareness, and support rehabilitation and social reintegration for people seeking to overcome drug dependence.

objectives.title: Key Objectives
objectives.lead: The National Operation is driven by four overarching strategic pillars to dismantle illicit trafficking, restore individuals, educate the next generation, and enforce institutional accountability.
objectives.cycleSubtitle: An integrated operational framework from interdiction to recovery and integrity
objectives.exploreTab: Select an Objective to explore details

items.title: Drug Prevention and Law Enforcement
items.description: Systematically disrupting illicit narcotics trafficking networks, intercepting sea and air supply routes, and enforcing zero-tolerance legal actions against organized cartels to eliminate drug availability across Sri Lanka.

actions.title: Dismantling Supply Chains
actions.desc: Targeting kingpins, regional distributors, and covert logistics networks through multi-agency intelligence.

actions.title: Maritime & Port Interdiction
actions.desc: 24/7 Naval coastal patrols and advanced high-energy container scanners at Colombo Port.

actions.title: Zero-Tolerance Law Enforcement
actions.desc: Special Task Force and Police Narcotics Bureau joint interdictions under strict statutory powers.

items.title: Rehabilitation and Reintegration
items.description: Providing evidence-based clinical detoxification, psychological counseling, and structured vocational training to empower individuals recovering from addiction to rebuild their lives and reintegrate into society with dignity.

actions.title: Evidence-Based Medical Detox
actions.desc: Expanding clinical treatment facilities across provincial and district hospitals with specialist care.

actions.title: Vocational Grants & Employment
actions.desc: Structured certifications and small-enterprise micro-grants to restore economic independence.

actions.title: Family & Community Reintegration
actions.desc: Compassionate psycho-social counseling and peer support networks to prevent relapse.

items.title: Public Awareness and Prevention
items.description: Mobilizing schools, universities, parents, and community leaders through intensive awareness programs and the anonymous 1818 hotline to build an informed society that actively rejects narcotic threats.

actions.title: School & Youth Empowerment
actions.desc: Life-skills education, anti-drug clubs, and student leadership councils in every educational zone.

actions.title: Hotline 1818 Anonymous Reporting
actions.desc: Encrypted, zero-log toll-free intelligence channel for confidential community reporting.

actions.title: Sports & Healthy Living Rallies
actions.desc: Islandwide marathon walks, youth sports tournaments, and community engagement campaigns.

items.title: Accountability and Institutional Integrity
items.description: Enforcing strict legal accountability against any public officials or corrupt individuals facilitating narcotics, confiscating illicit criminal proceeds, and preserving total forensic transparency across government institutions.

actions.title: Zero Tolerance for Complicity
actions.desc: Aggressive prosecution and dismissal of any corrupt state officials aiding drug networks.

actions.title: Asset Confiscation & Reinvestment
actions.desc: Tracing and seizing illicit wealth generated from narcotics to reinvest in citizen rehabilitation.

actions.title: Forensic & Whistleblower Shield
actions.desc: State-of-the-art laboratory evidence verification and robust statutory safeguards for tipsters.

header.title: A drug-free, safe Sri Lanka.
header.description: Sri Lanka’s united national initiative bringing together state institutions, security forces, and citizens to eradicate drug trafficking and safeguard future generations.

items.title: National Operation Against Drug Abuse Officially Inaugurated Under Presidential Patronage
items.description: The Government of Sri Lanka has formally inaugurated the 'Ratama Ekata' National Operation Against Drug Abuse, uniting law enforcement agencies, defense services, healthcare authorities, and civil society under a single strategic command. The comprehensive initiative focuses on disrupting organized narcotics trafficking networks, strengthening nationwide educational prevention in schools, and expanding state-funded medical rehabilitation pathways. The President reiterated that safeguarding the youth and building a secure, healthy, and drug-free nation remains the highest priority of the state.
items.author: Chamara Madushanka

items.title: Multi-Agency Taskforce Deploys Joint Intelligence Units Across Vulnerable Regional Corridors
items.description: In an intensive effort to dismantle illicit regional drug supply chains, a multi-agency taskforce comprising Sri Lanka Police, the Police Narcotics Bureau, and regional administrative intelligence desks has deployed specialized verification teams across key transport hubs and agrarian transit zones. The synchronized operations prioritize real-time tip-off investigations under strict Zero-Log anonymous protections.
items.author: Anuradhapura

items.title: Islandwide Community Outreach and Guidance Centers Established to Support Families Affected by Substance Abuse
items.description: Regional welfare directorates and agrarian community committees have launched integrated family support desks across the Southern Province. The centers provide compassionate psychological counseling, certified clinical referrals, and continuous social protection for families striving to overcome the impact of substance dependence.
items.author: Hambantota

items.title: 24 Specialized Officers Inducted to Direct Provincial Drug Prevention and Youth Wellness Programs
items.description: Twenty-four newly appointed prevention coordination officers formally received their induction credentials at the Governor's Office Auditorium in Anuradhapura. The officers will lead district-level educational seminars, oversee community rehabilitation linkages, and assist local law enforcement in eliminating local drug access points.
items.author: Chamara Madushanka

items.title: Central Operations Command and Citizen Intelligence Desk Go Live in Colombo
items.description: The Presidential Secretariat has inaugurated the new National Operations Centre and Citizen Media Bureau in Colombo, operating 24/7 communications consoles and encrypted intelligence routing protocols. The facility bridges public tip-offs received via Hotline 1818 with regional tactical response teams across the island.
items.author: Colombo

items.title: Regional Administrators and School Principals Convene for National Youth Protection Forum
items.description: Over 500 school principals, divisional secretaries, and youth counselors gathered in the North Western Province to establish coordinated substance abuse monitoring protocols for educational institutions. The symposium introduced early detection guidelines and certified peer-to-peer counseling programs.
items.author: Kurunegala

items.title: Navy and Coast Guard Intensify 24/7 Maritime Interdiction Patrols Along Territorial Waters
items.description: Sri Lanka Navy flotillas and Coast Guard interceptor units have expanded round-the-clock patrol operations across strategic maritime choke-points. Equipped with advanced surface radar and aerial reconnaissance, the squadrons maintain strict surveillance to intercept unauthorized offshore cargo transfers.
items.author: Trincomalee

items.title: 1,200 Student Ambassadors Mobilized Across 9 Provinces for Peer-to-Peer Substance Prevention
items.description: The National Youth Leadership Summit convened more than 1,200 student leaders from secondary schools and state universities in Colombo. Delegates launched campus awareness campaigns and signed a collective pledge advocating healthy, active, and drug-free university and school environments.
items.author: Colombo

items.title: State-of-the-Art Residential Rehabilitation and Psychological Healing Center Opened
items.description: The Ministry of Health and the National Dangerous Drugs Control Board commissioned a modern wellness facility in the Western Province. Offering zero-stigma confidential therapy, medical detoxification, and certified vocational training, the center helps individuals achieve long-term recovery and dignified social reintegration.
items.author: Gampaha

items.title: National Hotline 1818 Surpasses 10,000 Verified Citizen Tip-Offs with Zero-Log Confidentiality
items.description: Operational records indicate that the toll-free hotline 1818 has logged and evaluated over 10,000 verified citizen intelligence calls since launch. Operating under a strict Zero-Log privacy guarantee, the hotline has facilitated hundreds of targeted law enforcement interventions without endangering informants.
items.author: National Operations Desk

items.title: Accredited Vocational Toolkits and Entrepreneurship Grants Awarded to 150 Recovered Citizens
items.description: One hundred and fifty individuals who completed certified residential rehabilitation courses were awarded recognized technical certificates and starter equipment sets in electrical wiring, carpentry, and commercial organic farming to guarantee sustainable economic independence.
items.author: Kandy

items.title: Islandwide School Competition on Drug-Free Living Celebrates Creative Youth Contributions
items.description: The Ministry of Education concluded the national fine arts, essay writing, and public speaking competition celebrating drug-free youth culture. Thousands of students from all 25 administrative districts submitted original works promoting positive peer influence and substance prevention.
items.author: Colombo

items.title: Village Vigilance Committees Established Across Rural Secretariats to Eliminate Local Drug Outlets
items.description: Community elders, women's societies, and local agrarian leaders across the Eastern Province have formed village monitoring groups to safeguard rural communities. The committees collaborate with local authorities to eradicate covert narcotics distribution networks near farming settlements.
items.author: Ampara

items.title: Community Police Liaison Desks Formed in 45 Divisional Secretariats to Strengthen Safety
items.description: Sri Lanka Police has expanded community liaison desks across Galle and Matara to bridge neighborhood resident associations with law enforcement. The initiative enables swift reporting of suspicious activities and fosters trusted cooperation between citizens and police stations.
items.author: Galle

items.title: Comprehensive Medical Counseling and Substance Awareness Conducted in Plantation Districts
items.description: Mobile wellness teams visited plantation worker communities in the Nuwara Eliya and Badulla districts to conduct free health screenings, family mental wellness counseling, and educational workshops detailing the risks of illicit chemical substances.
items.author: Nuwara Eliya

items.title: Northern Province Wellness Sports Festival Promotes Drug-Free Lifestyle Among 2,000 Youths
items.description: Over 2,000 young athletes gathered at Duraiappah Stadium in Jaffna for the five-day Northern Province Sports Festival. Held under the banner of health and substance prevention, the event promoted teamwork and active athletic participation as shields against substance abuse.
items.author: Jaffna

items.title: High-Capacity Container Scanning Stations Activated at Colombo Port to Intercept Illicit Narcotics
items.description: Sri Lanka Customs has commissioned next-generation non-intrusive container radiographic scanners at the Colombo Port container terminal. The high-energy X-ray systems scan import containers in minutes, significantly improving border security against transnational contraband.
items.author: Colombo

items.title: Over 25,000 Anonymous Inquiries and Tip-Offs Processed Securely Under Strict Data Protection
items.description: The official citizen platform ratamaekata.gov.lk has handled more than 25,000 verified public reports and assistance requests. The portal utilizes end-to-end cryptographic safeguards to protect citizen anonymity while facilitating rapid operational response.
items.author: Presidential Secretariat

items.title: Farming Communities and Agrarian Societies Unite in National Pledge for Drug-Free Rural Villages
items.description: Agrarian development leaders and grassroots farmer organizations across Polonnaruwa and Monaragala have ratified a joint community accord pledging zero tolerance for illicit narcotics, while promoting healthy living and community vigilance.
items.author: Polonnaruwa

items.title: Women Leaders and Mothers' Societies Form National Network for Family-Centric Substance Prevention
items.description: Representatives from mothers' organizations and child protection officers met in Ratnapura to create grassroots intervention guidelines for families. The network offers early assistance to households dealing with youth substance abuse challenges.
items.author: Ratnapura

items.title: Tri-Forces and Police Special Task Force Execute Synchronized Readiness Drill Along Coastal Corridors
items.description: Army, Navy, Air Force, and Police Special Task Force units completed a joint interdiction simulation across coastal lagoon zones. The exercise tested rapid response command communications and tactical interception capabilities against offshore trafficking vessels.
items.author: Puttalam

items.title: Ministry of Health Opens Dedicated Medical Detoxification and Addiction Clinics Across 14 Base Hospitals
items.description: Specialized clinical outpatient facilities staffed by psychiatrists and medical officers were inaugurated in 14 district base hospitals across Uva and Sabaragamuwa provinces, providing free, compassionate, and confidential medical addiction therapies.
items.author: Badulla

items.title: 18 Regional Youth Wellness and Substance Prevention Counseling Units Established
items.description: Eighteen dedicated youth wellness facilities equipped with recreational resources, vocational mentoring, and qualified counselors opened in rural districts to provide safe spaces and life skills training for young people.
items.author: Matale

items.title: National Operation Against Drug Abuse Submits Q3 Progress Report Highlighting Major Enforcement Gains
items.description: The Advisory Council of the Ratama Ekata Operation presented its third-quarter report to the Presidential Secretariat, showing an 84% resolution rate for verified citizen tip-offs and a 40% rise in voluntary rehabilitation admissions nationwide.
items.author: Colombo
